newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Guoco says Manila Bay project above-board.
newsitem.headline: Guoco says Manila Bay project above-board.

text.p: Guoco Holdings (Philippines) Inc, a unit of Hong Kong's Guoco Group Ltd, said on Monday it remained confident that its Manila Bay reclamation project will be proven valid and above-board.

"We stand firm on our position that the contract is valid, fair and above-board," Guoco Holdings president Micky Yong told a news conference. "We did not bribe or coerce anybody in the government. We have gone through the normal process of securing the necessary permits and approvals for the project."

A senator has alleged that the contract to the Amari Coastal Bay Development Corp to reclaim and develop 750 square hectares of land in the Manila Bay was underpriced. The government is now in the process of reviewing the contract.
Guoco and its affiliate, Centennial City, are part of the Amari consortium. Italian Thai Development Plc is also a major shareholder.

"We have to admit, however, that the confidence of our creditors and investors had been badly affected by this controversy," Yong said. "We just hope that our case won't become a dangerous precedent for other legitimate local and foreign investors."
The land sharing arrangement with Public Estates Authority (PEA) is not grossly disadvantageous to the government, Yong said.

"The PEA will receive 43 percent of the 750 hectares gross area to be reclaimed or 20 percent of the net saleable area, complete with infrastructure and utilities, without contributing a single centavo toward the cost of reclamation and development estimated at 30 billion pesos," he said.
He also denied allegations that the land valuations were grossly understated at 1,250 pesos per square metre instead of 92,000 pesos per sq m.
"The 92,000 pesos refers to today's asking price for existing reclaimed commercial land along Manila Bay...," he said.

The 1,250 pesos per sq m pricing was based on three apparaisals made by independent appraisal companies conducted in early 1995 on three islands along Manila Bay which had been submerged in water, he said.

Yong said that Guoco is one of the more active foreign investors in the country over the last ten years, with 7.6 billion pesos worth of expansion projects in property, manufacturing, hotel and casino operations, and construction.
